# Independent Party and project-content values

These synthetic public-only literals define expectations for the first checked
Party and project-record value APIs. They cover both Party kinds, aliases and
details, all nine record kinds, six separate roles, every declared state,
exact tagged revisions and references, and date-versus-instant precision.

inputs.json contains only constructor inputs. oracle.json separately contains
independently authored decisions, complete typed projections, canonical bytes,
SHA-256 identities and trait expectations. Only the chosen case value may enter
the consumer. Expected answers never enter the value constructor. Constructors
borrow parsed values and return owned immutable data; input mutation cannot
change a returned value.

These cases qualify parsed-value shapes and pure typed values. A parsed value
cannot establish original UTF-8, duplicate-key rejection or original numeric
tokens. Actual transports retain their own complete raw decoding and resource
gates. References prove format, not canonical existence, current permission,
assent, agreement or actual persistence. Dates do not acquire midnight or a zone.

Public expectations precede implementation. No consumer output supplies a gold
answer. Canonical literals use only closed ASCII field names, strings, booleans,
arrays and objects; their complete UTF-8 values and digests are frozen here.
Ordinary builds/tests consume these committed files without another checkout.
The data is newly authored synthetic material under this repository's existing
MIT OR Apache-2.0 terms. It contains no customer or provider recordings.

See the [public schema](../../../../../contracts/public/v1/project-workflow.schema.json),
[workflow meaning](../../../../../docs/requirements/project-workflow.md),
[common values](../../../../../docs/requirements/common-contract.md) and
[verification contract](../../../../../docs/requirements/testing-and-coverage.md).
The manifest owns ordered case identities, bounds and public source pins.
